subject: Clarify SOC 2 Type II coverage for hybrid migration and private connector cutover
messages:
From: Jennifer Sullivan <jennifer.sullivan@bankcorp.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Cc: security-ops@bankcorp.com
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2027 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: SOC 2 Type II coverage: hosted -> private migration window and bridge letter

Hi Michael,

Quick question as we're preparing our vendor intake: our platform team is documenting the cutover for the pilot migration from Redwood hosted to a Private VPC-connected deployment. Cutover date was 2027-03-15.

1) Does Redwood's most recent SOC 2 Type II report (covering 2026-07-01 through 2026-12-31) and any bridge letter you can provide cover this hybrid timeline (hosted serving for initial traffic, then Private VPC after cutover)?
2) If not fully covered, can you provide a scoped bridge letter or attestation covering the specific controls that remained the same during the migration (network segmentation, encryption-in-transit, tenant isolation)?

We're also filling out a short SIG questionnaire and the auditors want clarity on what deployment modes are included by your report vs what would require a separate attestation.

Thanks,
Jennifer Sullivan
Senior Information Security Manager
BankCorp Financial

Attachments: network-request-outline.pdf (referenced)
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Jennifer Sullivan <jennifer.sullivan@bankcorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 09:14:42 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II coverage: hosted -> private migration window and bridge letter

Hi Jennifer — thanks for the clear note and timelines. Looping in Kim (security) and Karthik (audit/project) to confirm specifics and next steps.

Short answer: our standard Type II covers the hosted API and Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) configurations that were in production during the report period. Private deployments (customer-managed VPC/on-prem packages) are generally outside the scope of that report unless the Private deployment uses our managed Private offering with the components included in the attestation.

We can:
- Provide a bridge letter that scopes controls for the window around the migration if the controls in question were continuously in place (we can map control IDs to the migration artifacts).
- Provide the SOC 2 report PDF and a network topology snapshot showing isolation controls for the hosted traffic prior to cutover.

Kim and Karthik — can you confirm whether the customer used our managed Private package (which would be covered) or a fully customer-hosted on-prem build (which would not)? If it's the former we can include the Private environment components in the bridge; if the latter we should scope the bridge to the hosted timeframe and the handoff controls only.

Michael
VP, Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: SOC2-TypeII-2026-report.pdf (will attach in next message)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Jennifer Sullivan <jennifer.sullivan@bankcorp.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 03 Apr 2027 11:05:18 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II coverage: hosted -> private migration window and bridge letter

Jennifer, Michael — thanks for the ping. I'm confirming the technical boundaries here. A few points to make this explicit:

- "Hosted" (Redwood API) and "Dedicated" (our reserved GPU pools we operate) are in-scope for our latest Type II report. Controls around logical tenant isolation, encryption-in-transit, access provisioning, and change control for the serving runtime are included.
- Our "Private" product has two flavors: (A) Redwood-managed Private, where the control plane components and certain provisioning workflows remain operated by Redwood inside a customer VPC (this is eligible for inclusion in our SOC 2 under the managed private agreement), and (B) Customer-hosted / on-prem package where the customer runs the stack themselves — this is outside our attestation.

Looking at internal logs for deal BC-2027-084, Marissa — do you have a one-line summary of whether BankCorp signed for the Redwood-managed Private package or the self-hosted distribution? That will determine coverage.

If BankCorp used the managed Private, we can produce:
- A scoped bridge letter that extends the control mapping for the cutover window (we'll highlight any control differences).
- A short evidentiary bundle (config exports, network diagrams, and summary of deployment runbooks) aligned to the relevant SOC control IDs.

If customer-hosted, we can only attest to the hosted period and provide recommendations for the customer's independent evidence for the post-cutover environment.

I'll draft a bridge-letter outline once Marissa confirms the deployment flavor.

—Kim
Director, Security & Trust
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Jennifer Sullivan <jennifer.sullivan@bankcorp.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II coverage: hosted -> private migration window and bridge letter

Jennifer — quick confirmation from deal docs: BankCorp purchased the Redwood-managed Private package (contract signed 2027-02-28), with a managed control plane in their VPC and our on-call SREs performing deployments via the managed connector. The cutover on 2027-03-15 was executed by Redwood engineers over the managed connector.

Given that, we should be able to provide the bridge letter that maps the managed Private components into the attestation scope for the migration window. Kim — please proceed with the bridge-letter draft. Michael — I can surface the contract clause and the runbook excerpt if you want to include them in the evidentiary bundle.

Marissa
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: contract-summary-redwood-managed-private.pdf (referenced)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Jennifer Sullivan <jennifer.sullivan@bankcorp.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II coverage: hosted -> private migration window and bridge letter

Jennifer — thanks, Marissa — great.

I've attached a first-pass bridge-letter draft that: (a) confirms the Type II report for the hosted/Dedicated components, (b) lists the managed Private components we can include given the managed-control-plane model, and (c) proposes the migration window wording (2027-03-10 through 2027-03-20) to cover planning, cutover, and verification activities.

Key clarifications in the draft:
- Controls that map directly (access logging, key management references, change control tickets) will be covered as maintained by Redwood during the cutover.
- Controls that are operationally customer-run post-cutover (e.g., physical access, facility environmental controls for on-prem instances) are explicitly out of scope.
- Evidence bundle we will provide: the SOC 2 report (PDF), network topology PNG showing the managed connector, runbook excerpts, and exports of relevant audit logs for the migration window.

Next steps: Jennifer, if this aligns with your auditors' needs we can convert the draft to a signed bridge letter and upload the evidence bundle to the secure SharePoint link (or send via DocuSign as you prefer). Please confirm which controls your SIG/CAIQ reviewers want emphasized (we can include a control-to-question mapping).

Thanks,
Kim

Attachments: bridge-letter-draft.docx, SOC2-TypeII-2026-report.pdf, network-topology-drawings.png
